alex: Hey team — starting around 10:12 UTC I'm seeing a lot of 429s for requests to rwd-large-v2. These are batched inference requests with ~90k token contexts (system + history). No auth errors, API key is fine. Any ideas?
maria_support: Thanks for flagging — are the 429s coming back with a Retry-After header or body message? Also roughly how many concurrent requests and what's your requests-per-minute? :thinking_face:
alex: Body just says \"rate limit exceeded\". No Retry-After. TPS was spiking during load test: ~450 RPM overall to that model, and we had bursts of ~40 concurrent requests. Each request is a single POST with a 90k token context (we're doing long-document summarization).
ryan_runtime: Quick note: rwd-large-v2 has a per-model cap that is effectively applied: 600 RPM / 30k TPM and max concurrency 16 in the current infra tier. Large context sizes increase per-request token accounting; TPM counts input+output tokens. If you're doing ~90k input tokens per call that will blow through TPM very fast. Could be quota exhaustion under the hood; that often surfaces as 429s.
alex: Hmm that makes sense. We weren't aware TPM was being consumed by input tokens at that scale. Our billing dashboard doesn't show a hard billing block though — usage spiked but account wasn't suspended.
maria_support: Right — two separate protections: (1) per-model rate limits/TPM enforced at the serving layer (returns 429) and (2) account-level billing suspensions. Billing suspensions would return a clear auth/billing error. 429s here most likely mean either per-model RPM/TPM or the concurrency queue overflow.
ops-bot: Automated: ModelCapacityAlert rwd-large-v2 at 2026-03-17T10:14:03Z — concurrency peaked at 40, queue length exceeded threshold, dropping requests -> 429.
alex: Ok, repro steps I followed: curl POST /v1/generate -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -d '{"model":"rwd-large-v2","input":"<~90k tokens>"}'
